title: Arcs and angles at Kitt Peak
caption: The Milky Way arcing over the McMath-Pierce Solar Telescope, Kitt Peak National Observatory, Arizona
celestial: Photograph taken at Kitt Peak National Observatory, Arizona
credit: KPNO/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/P. Horálek (Institute of Physics in Opava)

recognition.text: NOIRLab Image of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The graceful arc of the Milky Way meets the sharp angles of the McMath-Pierce Solar Telescope in this night view of Kitt Peak National Observatory, near Tucson, Arizona. The telescope stands 33 meters tall, and its 60-meter angled shaft continues on underground.

The McMath-Pierce was once the largest solar telescope in the world. It worked with mirrors: the angled section sent sunlight down to a primary mirror 1.6 meters across. Now retired, it is being turned into an astronomy education center, Windows on the Universe, where visitors can explore research from Kitt Peak and observatories around the world, from optical and radio telescopes to gravitational-wave detectors.
The photographer, Petr Horálek, is one of NOIRLab’s Audiovisual Ambassadors, and his picture captures the old telescope at a turning point, still pointed at the sky it spent decades studying.

understand.summary: A ground-based landscape photograph credited to KPNO/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/P. Horálek (Institute of Physics in Opava). The source does not publish camera, exposure or color-processing details.
understand.eye: A camera can gather light for longer than the eye, so the Milky Way looks brighter and more detailed here than it would to someone standing on site.

explore: NOIRLab, the US National Science Foundation’s center for ground-based optical astronomy, runs Kitt Peak along with observatories in Chile and Hawai‘i. Its guiding motto is “Discovering Our Universe Together.”
alt: The curving band of the Milky Way rising over a tall, angular white telescope structure on a mountaintop.
